title: The earth
hook: Francis calls the earth sister and mother (Canticle of the Creatures)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was loving animals: care that reaches past our own kind. Your line was sister birds.

Brother Sun. Sister Moon. Brother Wind. Sister Water. Brother Fire. That's the cast list of a short song by Francis of Assisi, the Canticle of the Creatures. Tradition says he made it late in his life, when he was sick and his eyes were failing: a song in praise of the sun, from a man who could hardly see it. He goes through the whole family of creation, one relative at a time. Then he reaches the ground under everyone's feet, and gives it two names at once.
screen: `BROTHER SUN, SISTER MOON.` → `A WHOLE FAMILY OF CREATION.` → `TWO NAMES FOR THE GROUND.`

segments.voice: First, brother sun, sister water. In the Canticle, Francis praises God through each creature and gives each one a family name. The sun is a brother, beautiful and radiant. Water is a sister, useful, humble, precious and pure. The singer stands among the creatures as kin, not above them as owner. Second, our sister, mother earth. When Francis reaches the earth, one family word isn't enough. She's our sister, and our mother, who sustains us, governs us, and brings forth fruits and colored flowers and herbs. Sister: kin, alongside us. Mother: she feeds us. Third, to dress it and to keep it. Francis didn't invent this care. In Genesis, the first human is put in the garden of Eden with a job: "to dress it and to keep it." Tend it and guard it. And the Psalms add whose it is: "The earth is the LORD's, and the fulness thereof." In that picture, people are gardeners and keepers, not owners. Fourth, heaven under our feet. Henry David Thoreau, in Walden, writing about a pond in winter, put it this way: "Heaven is under our feet as well as over our heads." He wasn't a monk or a saint, but he arrived at a similar place: the ground is holy ground. Sister earth isn't an abstraction. It's the strip of grass by the bus stop, the window box, the park with the litter in it. Love for the earth starts with one patch of it.
screen: `BROTHER SUN, SISTER WATER.` · `OUR SISTER, MOTHER EARTH.` · `TO DRESS IT AND TO KEEP IT.` · `HEAVEN UNDER OUR FEET.` · then, large: `SISTER EARTH.`

segments.voice: Put your feet flat on the floor and feel your weight settle through them, down past the floor and the building to the soil, and rest your attention there for a few breaths. Then let one patch of ground you pass often come to mind, a tree pit, a yard, a roadside strip, and see it clearly, litter and all, the way a keeper would. If you pray, you can give thanks to God for the earth beneath you.
The earth. The ground that Francis called our sister and our mother, that Genesis gives people to dress and keep, and that Thoreau found heaven in. Today's word.
Your line: sister earth. Kin under your feet, and a keeper's work in your hands. Day eight hundred sixty-six, done.

howItsDone: Christians sing and pray Francis's Canticle of the Creatures, and some churches and communities hold creation-care days, garden work and cleanups; Jews and Christians read Genesis 2 as a call to tend and keep the earth.

chat.meaning: In the Canticle the earth is our sister, kin alongside us, and our mother who sustains us. Genesis gives the first human the job to dress it and keep it.

Francis of Assisi.meaning: an Italian friar known for his love of all creatures

Canticle of the Creatures.meaning: Francis's song praising God through sun, moon, wind, water, fire and earth

Eden.meaning: the garden where Genesis places the first humans

Thoreau.meaning: an American writer who lived simply by Walden Pond

Walden.meaning: Thoreau's book about living simply beside a pond
